title: Ledgerline billing service: codebase map
scenario: Codebase architecture and source mapping: a hand-written map of a billing service's invoice path that mixes verified code facts (file, symbol, line range), the author's architectural interpretation, one probable-but-unconfirmed relationship and several explicit unknowns.
audience: Engineers joining the billing team who need to find their way from a component to its file and symbol
objective: See the invoice path as components wired by labelled calls, reads, writes and publishes, each traceable to its file and symbol, while telling verified facts, interpretation, inference and unknowns apart.

units.quote: This note maps the invoice path of the Ledgerline billing service as of commit `a41c9e2`.
I read the code by hand; nothing here was generated by a tool.

omittable.note: How the map was made, not what it says about the code.

units.quote: Every statement says how I know it: "the code does" means I read it in the file named, "my reading" is my own interpretation, "probably" means I suspect it but did not confirm it, and "unknown" means I looked and could not find out.

omittable.note: A reading legend. Its effect is checked through the certainty markers on the cards themselves, not by repeating the legend.

units.quote: Refunds, dunning and the customer portal are out of scope.
`billing/invoices` holds the entry point, the draft type and the write to the invoice tables.
`billing/usage` turns raw usage events into usage lines.
`billing/pricing` turns usage lines into priced lines.
`billing/tax` wraps the external tax provider.
`billing/events` publishes billing events for other services to consume.
Each module exposes its functions through its own `index.ts` file.
The modules import each other only through those index files; I found no import that reaches into another module's internal files.
The code defines `generateInvoice(accountId, period)` in `billing/invoices/generate.ts`, lines 12–58.

critical.note: The entry point's file, symbol and line range: the anchor of the whole map.

units.quote: It is the only exported function in that file.
The admin console's "Regenerate invoice" action calls it from `billing/admin/regenerate.ts`.
`generateInvoice` does its work in a fixed order.
First, the code calls `collectUsage(accountId, period)` to get the usage lines for the period.

critical.note: A verified call edge of the entry point.

units.quote: Second, it calls `priceUsage(lines, plan)` to turn those lines into priced lines.

critical.note: A verified call edge of the entry point.

units.quote: Third, it calls `TaxClient.quote(draft)` to get the tax for the draft invoice.

critical.note: A verified call edge of the entry point.

units.quote: Finally, it writes the invoice and publishes an event, as described under "Persistence and events" below.
The code in `billing/usage/collect.ts` defines `collectUsage(accountId, period)`.
It reads the `usage_events` table, selecting the account's rows whose `occurred_at` falls inside the period, and groups them by meter into usage lines.

critical.note: The direction of the read (collectUsage reads usage_events) must survive.

units.quote: Events flagged `is_test` are skipped.
It does not write to any table.
The code in `billing/pricing/priceUsage.ts` defines `priceUsage(lines, plan)`.
It reads the `price_plans` table through a helper in the same file, `loadPlan(planId)`, and multiplies each line's quantity by the plan's unit price.
Prices are held as integer cents throughout, never as floating-point amounts.
`priceUsage` probably also reads the `discounts` table.

critical.note: An inferred relationship: it may be shown only as unconfirmed, never as a fact.

units.quote: The file imports a helper called `discountFor`, and the name suggests a discount lookup, but I did not find a call site and have not confirmed that it ever runs.
Treat this link as unconfirmed until someone traces it.
The code in `billing/tax/client.ts` defines a `TaxClient` class whose `quote(draft)` method sends the draft invoice to an external tax provider, Taxwell, over HTTPS.
The request has a timeout of 8 seconds, set on line 21.
The API key is read from the `TAXWELL_API_KEY` environment variable when the client is constructed.
The response carries a tax amount for each line, which `generateInvoice` adds to the draft before saving it.
How retries work for the tax provider is not documented.

critical.note: An explicit unknown: it must be shown as unknown and never filled in with an invented retry policy.

units.quote: `TaxClient.quote` contains no retry code, and I could not find out whether its callers retry, whether the Taxwell client library retries on its own, or what happens to the invoice when a quote times out.
The code writes the finished invoice to two tables, `invoices` and `invoice_lines`, inside one database transaction in `billing/invoices/generate.ts`, lines 44–52.

critical.note: The write edge and its one-transaction condition.

units.quote: If either insert fails, the transaction rolls back and neither row is kept.
The `invoices` row is written with the status `finalized`; I found no code path that writes any other status.
After the transaction commits, `generateInvoice` calls `publishInvoiceFinalized(invoice)` in `billing/events/publish.ts`.

critical.note: Publishing happens only after the commit.

units.quote: That function publishes an `invoice.finalized` message to the `billing-events` topic.
The payment and email services subscribe to that topic; I did not read their code.
What happens when publishing fails after the commit is unknown.

critical.note: An explicit unknown on the publish step.

units.quote: The code logs the error and returns, so an invoice can exist without its event, but I found no job that re-sends missed events and no note saying whether one is planned.
The draft passed between the steps has this shape, defined in `billing/invoices/types.ts`:
`taxCents` stays undefined until `TaxClient.quote` returns.
I did not read the definitions of `BillingPeriod` and `PricedLine`.
My reading is that `billing/pricing` acts, in effect, as the pricing boundary: as far as I could see, no code outside it reads `price_plans`, so a pricing change should only need edits there.
This is an interpretation of the current structure, not a rule the code enforces; nothing stops another module from querying `price_plans` directly.

critical.note: The boundary is the author's interpretation, not an enforced rule.

units.quote: In the same spirit, `generateInvoice` behaves like an orchestrator.
It holds no pricing or tax logic of its own and only sequences the calls, which is why it reads so short for the work it starts.
What starts the regular monthly run? The admin action is clear, but I could not find the scheduler that calls `generateInvoice` for every account.

critical.note: The monthly trigger is unknown; no scheduler may be invented.

units.quote: Does `priceUsage` really apply discounts? See the unconfirmed link above.
Who owns the `billing-events` topic? No owner is listed in the repository.
Why does the `invoices` table have a status column if every row is written as `finalized`? It may be reserved for drafts, but nothing in the code says so.
In short, the verified invoice path is a fixed sequence inside `generateInvoice`: collect usage, price it, quote tax, write both invoice tables in one transaction, then publish `invoice.finalized`.

critical.note: The verified path in one line.

units.quote: Two parts of the map are not verified: the discounts read is only probable, and the tax provider's retry behaviour is unknown.

critical.note: The takeaway carries its own uncertainty.

safeToOmit.why: How the map was made and how to read it; the certainty markers themselves are checked on the cards.

provenance.note: Original text written for this dataset. The Ledgerline service, the Taxwell provider, every path, symbol, table, line range, commit id, timeout and environment variable are invented and describe no real codebase.
